items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I know at one time Bennie Moten left Kansas City and came to New York. And he made it real big with what they call a two four beat...

ctx.x: Coming up being born in Oklahoma, which was the southwest at that time, can you describe for us how the southwest sound, like the Count Basie sound, was different from the sounds on the east coast or the west coast?

Oh yeah, well it was different but I mean I don’t know how I can explain to you the difference because in fact the Kansas City was different from any of the styles. Boys would come up from the south and Texas and Louisiana and all through there but they’d come through Kansas City and they changed their style somewhere. Because anytime you would tell somebody you’re from Kansas City, they know that you are a good musician. If you’ve got the Kansas City stamp you’ve got it made. I can’t tell you. It’s different but…

One other thing I would like to ask and that is you know the violin, for most people is considered a classical instrument. What things do you do with your fingers, with your phrasing, with your articulations to convert that instrument to a jazz sound? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
